subject: [PATCH v6 03/12] mm: add PMD swap entry splitting support

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David (Arm) noted that setting freeze=false after a VM_WARN_ON_ONCE() is inconsistent, and suggested refactoring the 'freeze' flag handling to make it clear when migration entries are being used.

Reviewer David suggested renaming 'sl_entry' to a more descriptive name, specifically 'pmd_swp_entry' or 'swp_entry', and also 'pte_swp_entry' for consistency.
reviews.raw_body:
It's odd to VM_WARN_ON_ONCE() and then set freeze=false;

I'd just add the comment above the VM_WARN_ON_ONCE() and drop the =false.

freeze=true really only applies during page migration, where swap entries don't
apply.

I think it's time to clean that up ... that is

a) Expose a helper called split_pmd_to_migration_entries() that is only used by
code that installs migration entries.

b) Hide that "freeze" flag from all other file-external functions

c) Rename the boolean to "use_migration_entries"

Then it's rather clear in this code that this should never happen.

---

No existing code uses "sl_entry". Maybe just call it "pmd_swp_entry"/"swp_entry"
and below "pte_swp_entry".



Apart from that nothing jumped at me :)

-- 
Cheers,

David

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch adds support for splitting PMD swap entries into 512 PTE swap entries in the Linux kernel's memory management (mm) module. This is done by adding a new branch to the __split_huge_pmd_locked() function that checks if the PMD entry is a swap entry and, if so, splits it into individual PTEs. The patch also updates the folio_remove_rmap_pmd() gate to correctly handle present THP splits. This change allows for more efficient handling of large pages in memory management scenarios involving swapping.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a need to make the migration choice private by restructuring the code in v2
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks! I have done this now for next revision. The migration choice is now private as
use_migration_entries, the normal split APIs no longer expose it, and the rmap migration
path uses split_pmd_to_migration_entries().

m

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary:
The reviewer noted that pmd_present() considers PMDs cleared by pmdp_invalidate() as present, which could lead to incorrect handling of migration entries on x86 architecture.

Reviewer noted that the VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(pmd_is_swap_entry(old_pmd)) check in the !vma_is_anonymous() branch is missing, which could lead to unexpected behavior if pmd_is_swap_entry(old_pmd) returns true.
reviews.raw_body:
Hm. On x86, pmd_present() recognises !_PAGE_PRESENT | _PAGE_PSE PMDs as
present. Other archs do similar thing. pmdp_invalidate() clears present
bit, but keeps PSE around, so it is present from SW PoV.

pmd_is_migration_entry() should work correctly on pmdp_invalidate()ed
entries.

---

PTL protects us from value drifting under us if compiler decides to load
it multiple times, right? Same pattern as the migration/device-private
branches above, so not a new concern, just checking.

BTW, do we want VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(pmd_is_swap_entry(old_pmd)) in
!vma_is_anonymous() branch to avoid surprises?

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(freeze) is compiled out without DEBUG_VM, and the freeze = false assignment prevents swap entries from being processed by reclaim paths, but this would break in production builds; they suggested setting folio and page to NULL instead.
reviews.raw_body:
VM_WARN_ON_ONCE() is compiled out without DEBUG_VM. The freeze = false is
what actually keeps the swap entry out of

      if (freeze || pmd_is_migration_entry(old_pmd)) {
              ...
              make_writable_migration_entry(page_to_pfn(page + i));

and out of the put_page(page) below it, where page is uninitialized in the
swap branch. Dropping it leaves nothing on production builds.

If freeze = false goes, folio and page must be set to NULL there (or
something along the lines).

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the current implementation of PMD swap entry splitting support is overly cautious and suggested restructuring the code for clarity, while also expressing concern about adding unnecessary code.
reviews.raw_body:
Right, because it's a condition you shouldn't hit on production builds.

And I raised how we can restructure the code to make it clear that we are being
overly cautions here.

Let's not add unnecessary code just because the existing code is hard to follow.

-- 
Cheers,

David
